goal:
Investigate what can we do better with this CPU-only program! I intend to make my engine the fastest inference both prefill and decode on CPU only. Use this command when you're trying to use it:
cargo run -r -- -m ~/Documents/Models/openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B/model-00000-of-00001.safetensors --template ~/Documents/Models/openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B/chat_template.jinja "Who are you?"
refinedGoal: Optimize TinyMiniGo (from-scratch Rust inference engine for MiniCPM5-1B) to be as fast as possible on CPU-only hardware (AMD Ryzen 7 5800H, AVX2+FMA, 8C/16T), for both prefill and decode. Constraints: keep the hand-rolled math identity (std threads + explicit SIMD intrinsics allowed; no BLAS/ML-framework crates); greedy generation output must match the current/HF reference text; weights stay BF16 end-to-end with in-kernel dequantization. Add a benchmark mode to measure prefill tok/s and decode tok/s so every step is verifiable. Baseline: ~51s wall / ~1 tok/s decode for 47 tokens with a 13-token prompt.

tasks.auditResult: All 7 tasks verified against their acceptance criteria with live execution, not just code inspection. (1) Timing instrumentation prints load/prefill/decode tok/s to stderr; scripts/bench.sh and BENCHMARK.md baseline recorded. (2) Batched forward_seq prefill: measured 59.2 tok/s vs 1.4 baseline (~42x, exceeds >5x). (3) AVX2+FMA kernels with runtime detection + scalar fallback, precomputed RoPE tables, fused MLP; decode 12.31 tok/s (>3x target); a broken horizontal-sum was caught by the md5 output gate and fixed. (4) std::thread::scope parallelism over output rows with measured thresholds; documented finding that 16-thread gemv is slower due to DRAM contention. (5) Flat contiguous per-layer KV cache [pos x kv_dim], attention reads directly with GQA head-slicing, no per-head copies or per-token allocations. (6) BF16 raw-bit weights with exact in-register dequant (shift<<16); RSS 2.57GB (halved from 4.3GB); f32 fallbacks kept. (7) BENCHMARK.md has a complete before/after log and key findings; README performance/architecture notes updated; wall time 7.04s vs 51s baseline. No BLAS/ML crates in Cargo.toml; hand-rolled math identity preserved. Two stretch targets (>=15 tok/s decode, >20x wall) were not literally hit but are documented as such in BENCHMARK.md; all hard criteria — byte-identical greedy output, passing tests, and large verified prefill/decode/memory improvements — are met. Approved.

result:
Optimized TinyMiniGo (from-scratch Rust MiniCPM5-1B CPU inference engine) for prefill and decode speed on AVX2 CPU, keeping the hand-rolled math identity (std threads + runtime-detected AVX2/FMA intrinsics, no BLAS/ML crates).

Results on the reference command (Ryzen 7 5800H, greedy):
- Prefill: 1.4 → 57-71 tok/s (~44×)
- Decode: 1.39 → 12.3 tok/s (~8.8×)
- Wall: 51 s → 7.2 s
- Peak memory: 4.3 GB → 2.57 GB
- Output text byte-identical to baseline (md5-gated every step); all numerical tests vs transformers reference pass.

Changes shipped (each verified with cargo test + md5 output gate):
1. Benchmark harness: timing instrumentation (load/prefill/decode tok/s on stderr), scripts/bench.sh, BENCHMARK.md with baseline.
2. Batched prefill: forward_seq processes the whole prompt with batched matmul + causal batched attention.
3. SIMD kernels: AVX2+FMA dot products (runtime-detected, scalar fallback), precomputed RoPE tables, fused SiGLU, allocation-free decode hot path. Found and fixed a broken AVX2 horizontal-sum that produced wrong logits (caught by the output-hash gate).
4. std-thread parallelism over output rows: batched gemm uses all cores; decode gemv uses cores/4 after measuring that full-core gemv is slower (DRAM contention).
5. Contiguous flat KV cache per layer ([pos, kv_dim]) — zero per-token KV allocations, no per-head copies in attention.
6. BF16 weights end-to-end: raw bf16 bits stored in WMat, dequantized in-register in the gemv/gemm kernels (bit-exact), halving memory bandwidth; embed/norm tables stay f32; f32 fallback paths kept for tests and non-BF16 models.
7. Docs: BENCHMARK.md optimization log with key findings and remaining ideas; README performance + architecture notes updated.

Also added tests/diff_debug.rs (forward_seq vs forward_token consistency), fixed the kv-cache unit tests for the new flat API, and cleaned all compiler warnings.
